- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% in subsequent 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.3) or shows strong divergence from prior trend, model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–4% to counteract mean reversion bias.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; for 30-day forecasts, smooth transitions using 3–5 day moving average of sentiment-weighted history.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65–70), model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted to align with 2–3 day moving average of recent low.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating 0.0–1.0), model often fails to capture sentiment-driven corrections; apply sentiment-weighted smoothing: 0.7×prior + 0.3×current sentiment to adjust forecast weights.
